mismatch_reasons.build_split_from_test: command-normalizer lumped tsc/npm run build/bundle into family test; the registry splits them into build
mismatch_reasons.build_bare_substring_tokens_dropped: legacy build matched bare dist/artifact/bundle substrings (e.g. Write-Output lines about artifacts became BUILD->PASS); the registry keeps only real build-tool commands and the command falls back to its true family
mismatch_reasons.clusters_legacy_split: no-capability-clusters reported project_test_or_build; the registry resolves test|build per command
mismatch_reasons.clusters_missing_family: no-capability-clusters had no enumeration/build/dom family, so those commands were unknown there; the registry classifies them
mismatch_reasons.pattern_unified: no-capability-clusters used broader sql/process patterns (bare tokens like "sql"); the registry keeps the stricter command-normalizer patterns and the command returns to its true family
mismatch_reasons.dom_word_boundary: no-capability-clusters matched dom as a substring (e.g. Get-Random); the registry requires word boundaries
mismatch_reasons.tsc_substring_false_positive: the legacy test family matched bare "tsc" inside paths and filenames (tsconfig.json was read constantly in this corpus, e.g. "Get-Content tsconfig.json" became TEST->PASS); the registry anchors tool names to command position, so these return to their true family
mismatch_reasons.family_order_unified: the legacy classifiers checked families in different orders (normalizer: process before http; clusters: http before process), so hybrid commands resolved differently; the registry keeps the normalizer order
mismatch_reasons.meta_promoted_for_clustering: no-capability-clusters reported unknown; the registry classifies write/read/search/meta as canonical families
mismatch_reasons.legacy_rename: same family, legacy id renamed by the alias map
